overall.summary: All record numbers, closed forms, counts and the 78 claims reproduce; weakened on shape and scope wording: the ST depression gate is described as 'uneven' and 'mainly' above 1.2 mm when it is a clean hinge, the 'only if not downsloping' rule fails at high ST depression, the 147 bpm threshold holds only with non-anginal chest pain, and one heart-rate-gate evidence sentence is a whole-model contrast the part barely contributes to.

findings.statement: raises the predicted risk with ST depression on exercise, in an uneven way
findings.check: probe --sweep oldpeak=0:3:16 (typical); per-patient fold points from the closed form
findings.evidence: the part's shape is a clean hinge: exactly zero up to about 1.23 mm for the typical patient (risk 11.9% flat from 0 to 1.2 mm), then a straight rise in the score (+0.16 per 0.2 mm, 13.3% at 1.4 mm to 35.9% at 3.0 mm). 'Uneven' does not name this shape; it should read 'changes nothing until about 1.2 mm, then raises it steadily'. Direction and thal:7 amplification are right.

findings.statement: raises the risk in an uneven way, mainly once it rises above about 1.2 mm (between 0.2 and 1.2 mm for different patients); 12% at 0 mm to 32% at 2.8 mm
findings.evidence: numbers reproduce (11.9% -> 32.3%, fold 1.23 mm), but the part does nothing at all below the fold ('mainly' understates 'only'), and the rise above it is steady, not uneven. Folds among non-downsloping patients are 0.11, 0.17 or 1.23 mm (12 patients always past it); downsloping patients fold at 2.9 to 5.1 mm, outside the stated range. Same wording recurs in drafted.blocks[1] sentences 1-2, readdown.ann_32.evidence[2-3], readdown.ann_35.evidence[1] and worth_checking[5].

findings.statement: raises the risk only if the ST segment does not slope down; with a downsloping segment the risk stays at about 42%
findings.evidence: true over 0 to 2.8 mm (typical risk flat at 41.6%), but inside the data support (oldpeak up to 6.2 mm) the part switches on for downsloping patients too: typical downsloping patient 41.6% at 5.0 mm, 49.1% at 5.5, 59.1% at 6.0 mm; 4 of the 17 downsloping training patients have the part active (4 of 7 with oldpeak >= 3 mm). 'Only if' is an overclaim; 'only at very high ST depression' is what the model does.

findings.statement: fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL, a fixed thallium defect and typical angina all lower the predicted risk
findings.evidence: the model genuinely does this (claims reproduce), but each conflicts with clinical knowledge (diabetes and fixed perfusion defects are risk factors; typical angina is the most suggestive symptom). The explanation already flags these; listed here for the domain reviewer.

findings.statement: a downsloping ST segment suppresses the ischaemia gate
findings.evidence: downsloping ST is clinically the most worrying slope; the model's -1.08 slope:3 weight in the gate is real (17 patients), and the explainer says so. Flag only.

findings.statement: plain and technical hypotheses are stated in domain terms
findings.evidence: all three gates are described by what they do to the prediction and for whom (ischaemia evidence; women with exercise angina lose their sex protection; high heart rate with non-anginal pain protective); none merely restates the closed form
